chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who had two slave sisters and had relations with one of them, then had relations with the other.
He said: “If he has relations with the other one, then the first becomes prohibited to him until the other dies.”
I said: “What do you think—if he sells her, does the first become permissible for him?”
He said: “If he sold her out of a need, and nothing concerning the other occurs in his mind, then I see no harm in that. But if he sells her in order to return to the first, then no, and no honor.”
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man has relations with two bondwomen who are sisters and then sells one of them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a man who owns two bondwomen who are sisters and has relations with both. It states that once he has relations with the second, the first becomes prohibited to him until the second dies, and that selling the second only affects the ruling if the sale was done for a genuine need rather than as a device to return to the first.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4551 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
I asked him about a man who owned two slave sisters and had relations with one of them, then later had relations with the other.
Imam (as) said: "If he has relations with the second one, then the first becomes prohibited for him until the second one dies."
I said: "What if he sells the second one? Does the first then become permissible for him?"

Imam (as) said: "If he sold her due to a need and without intending to return to the first one, then I see no harm in it. But if he sold her with the intention of returning to the first one, then no, and may he have no honor in doing so."
